briefFidelity: FAIL. The brief asks for a COLONY — cells radiating from a shared centre, each generation budding from the last, biological rather than geometric, accretion not design. Before I had read a word of it I reached for 'medallion', 'emblem', 'wreath', 'ship's wheel', 'rosette', 'annulus', 'pinwheel' and 'rotational symmetry'. That is the exact vocabulary the brief rules out: these read as heraldic devices, struck and finished, not as things that grew. Nothing in the twelve shows generational structure — there are no discrete rounded cells, no overlapping clusters, no successive rings where a later generation visibly buds off an earlier one. The members are curved blades in a single radial array around a core, which is one gesture repeated, i.e. design. The one genuine hit is the palette: sage/teal verdigris and cream/bone over deep ink, damp and mineral, exactly as asked, with no stray hue. But palette alone cannot carry a subject the forms contradict.
seedVariation: MIXED, with degenerate members at both ends. Judged on the 120px sheet: the twelve are not one work twelve times — 9011, 10622, 10980, 10264, 10443 and 9906 are genuinely different objects (layered wreath, cream disc with dark core, tile-ring, broken ring). But the spread runs off the end of the scale in the wrong way. 9190 renders NOTHING — a blank panel at 256, at 120, and in all three market conditions. 9369 and 10801 are flat unmodulated green blobs that are close to interchangeable at browse size, and 9369 was the seed chosen for the 512px hero, where it is a plain sage polygon with a ragged edge and zero interior. An empty token and a featureless blob are not 'a colony that has not spread far'; they are members with no work in them, and this commitment is permanent.
thumbnailSurvival: PARTIAL. About half the set holds its identity at 120px, and it holds only by silhouette — a hole in the middle, a light rim against a dark core, a broken edge. All interior blade detail is gone at browse size in every one of the twelve. The other half collapses: 9369 and 10801 are the same green dot, 10085 is a green dot with a pale smudge, 9548 is a green dot with a faint swirl, 9727 nearly disappears into the ground, and 9190 is an empty tile.
marketResponse: FAIL, and this is the decisive failure. The brief makes growth and retreat the whole story — recovery pushes the colony outward and multiplies its members, stress pulls it back toward the centre and reduces it — and requires the change to be plainly visible at thumbnail size. Unprompted at stage 1, before reading any of that, I wrote that the changes are 'small and internal' and that 'the market-condition differences are not visible at all at 120px'. Neither claimed axis moves: the outer radius of every token is essentially fixed across all three conditions, and the member COUNT never changes — no element is added in recovery or removed in stress. What does move is the wrong quantity and, where legible, the wrong direction: 9548's blades get WIDER and flip from near-black to sage under stress, and 9011's outer petals grow and rotate under stress, so the visible reading is expansion under stress. 9369 changes only the jaggedness of its perimeter, invisible at 256 and absent at 120. 9190 cannot respond at all. A transformation that is the entire premise of the piece is not present.
tokenIdentity: PASS, and it is the strongest column. Every token is unmistakably the same object across neutral, stress and recovery — 9011 stays that camo-banded wreath, 9548 stays that bladed disc, nothing morphs into a different creature. If anything the stability is excessive: identity is preserved by the transform being too small to see, which is the same fact that fails the market column rather than a separate virtue.
composition: Competent but thin, and it never uses the frame. Every token is one centred medallion floating in a large empty margin; the frame is a void, not a compositional element, and there is no tension, no off-centre weight, no edge relationship anywhere in twelve tokens. Focal hierarchy is genuinely good on the dense members (10622 and 9011 read rim, then core, then blade cluster, then perimeter studs, in that order). No clipping. The artifacts are at the ends of the density range: 9369's only incident is aliased notching on its perimeter, which reads as a rendering edge rather than an intended contour, and the low-coverage members (9727, 9906) are so sparse the composition is a single outline with an empty interior.
reasoning: My stage-1 description named this a set of centred heraldic medallions in verdigris and bone, differing mainly in how much of a fixed layer stack each one draws, and changing only slightly and internally between conditions. The brief asks for a biological colony that grows outward and retreats visibly at thumbnail size. Two of the three things the brief cares about are missing: the forms read as struck geometry rather than accretion, with no budding, no generations and no discrete cells; and the growth/retreat transformation — which the brief calls the whole market story and requires to be plainly visible at browse size — is not visible at browse size at all, does not change radius or member count in either direction, and where it is visible at 256px it appears to expand under stress. Only the palette lands. Set against that, one token that renders as an empty frame in every seed and every condition, and a 512px hero that is a flat green polygon, are not marginal blemishes; they are permanent members of a fixed collection. This is not a refusal over taste — the dense medallions are handsome and the colour discipline is real. It is a refusal because the object described is not the object commissioned, and because the claimed transformation cannot be seen.
wouldChange: Make the market response BE the biology, and make it happen in the silhouette. Replace the single radial array of blades with discrete rounded cells accreting in successive generational rings from the centre, so that recovery literally adds a generation — a new outer ring of members, a larger overall radius — and stress removes one, shrinking the colony back toward the core. That single change fixes both gates at once: the forms start reading as growth rather than as a struck emblem, and the transform becomes a change in outer diameter and member count, which is the one kind of change that still survives at 120px. Fix the degenerate seeds in the same pass — no token may render empty, and a minimum of one visible generation must always be drawn.
